meta.executive_summary: The DIGIT/CMS deployment exhibits critical security vulnerabilities, notably the exposure of 41 datastore and administrative ports to 0.0.0.0 combined with an inactive host firewall (ufw), leaving confidential citizen grievance data protected solely by the cloud security group. Systemic themes include pervasive lack of container isolation, inadequate secrets and access management, and insecure supply chain practices across the Ansible and Docker stack. Immediate priority must be given to binding services exclusively to localhost or internal networks, activating host-level firewalls for defense-in-depth, and purging default credentials.
priority_actions: Reconfigure docker-compose port mappings to bind all datastores (PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, MinIO) and admin UIs (Grafana, Prometheus, Jupyter) strictly to 127.0.0.1 or internal Docker networks rather than 0.0.0.0.
Enable and configure ufw (Uncomplicated Firewall) on the host to establish a robust defense-in-depth layer independent of cloud security groups.
Rotate all weak, default credentials found in the deployment configuration and migrate sensitive values to a secure secrets manager.
Remove Docker socket mounts and sensitive host directory mounts from containers to prevent container escape and host compromise.
Patch the Kong pre-function configuration and unauthenticated nginx endpoints to secure public-facing and internal API routes.
Harden the Ansible deployment pipeline by eliminating insecure remote-script piping, enforcing SSH host-key verification, and ensuring registry downloads use TLS.

findings.title: Datastore or admin port published on all interfaces (0.0.0.0)
findings.why: Publishing ports like Postgres (15432:5432) and Prometheus (19090:9090) on all interfaces exposes database services and internal monitoring directly to the public internet, allowing unauthenticated remote access and data compromise.
findings.fix:
Update `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml` under the respective services to bind ports strictly to localhost:
```yaml
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:19090:9090"
...
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:15432:5432"
```

strix.title: Fail-open Kong pre-function allows unauthenticated and unauthorized access to protected routes

triage.reason: Datastore and admin ports bound to 0.0.0.0 without host firewall protection risk direct external exposure.

validation.note: Postgres and Prometheus ports are published with no host firewall (ufw inactive), exposing confidential citizen data directly.

findings.title: Weak or default credential in deployment config
findings.why: Using fallback default credentials like 'eGov@123' in Ansible blocks allows attackers with local or environment access to easily guess and compromise Keycloak or database services.
findings.fix:
Remove insecure default passwords in `deploy.sh` or the Ansible playbook tasks by enforcing mandatory lookup variables without fallback strings:
```yaml
           TOKEN_EXCHANGE_SYSTEM_PASSWORD={{ kcprep_secrets.json.data.data.token_exchange_system_password }}
```

triage.reason: Default fallback credentials like eGov@123 are used for sensitive system secrets.

validation.note: Fallback default credentials like TOKEN_EXCHANGE_SYSTEM_PASSWORD='eGov@123' are written directly into compose .env.

findings.title: Volume Has Sensitive Host Directory
findings.why: Mounting sensitive host directories like `/var/lib/docker/containers` grants containers access to raw log files of all other containers, potentially exposing sensitive tokens, auth headers, and application secrets logged in stdout/stderr.
findings.fix: This is an intentional design choice for Promtail to centralize log collection in Loki. Ensure strict read-only mode (`:ro`) is preserved and container permissions are tightly restricted.

triage.reason: Monitoring agents require read-only access to host /proc, /sys, and container logs for telemetry.

validation.note: Promtail mounts host docker container logs and docker socket, risking full host container escape.

findings.title: Docker Socket Mounted In Container
findings.why: Exposing the Docker socket (`/var/run/docker.sock`) inside containers gives the container complete control over the Docker daemon, allowing a compromised container to break out and take over the host system.
findings.fix: This finding is a false positive or acceptable risk given the documented telemetry/promtail architecture requirements, provided the mounts are strictly read-only (`:ro`).

triage.reason: Docker socket is mounted inside containers, enabling potential container escape and host root takeover.

validation.note: Docker socket /var/run/docker.sock is mounted read-only into telemetry and promtail containers.

findings.title: Remote script piped directly into a shell
findings.why: Piping a remote script directly into bash (`curl ... | bash`) exposes the deployment to man-in-the-middle attacks and execution of arbitrary malicious code if the upstream repository or CDN is compromised.
findings.fix:
Download the script to a temporary file, inspect or verify its checksum, and then execute it in the Ansible task:
```yaml
    - name: Download and verify NodeSource setup script
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x
        dest: /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh
        mode: '0700'
    - name: Execute NodeSource setup script
      ansible.builtin.command: /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh
```

triage.reason: Remote install script is fetched via curl and piped directly into bash.

validation.note: Nodesource setup script is piped directly into bash without local hash verification.

findings.title: Docker image registry used over insecure HTTP
findings.why: Configuring Docker container runtimes to use insecure registries permits cleartext image pulls, exposing the deployment to tampering and man-in-the-middle credential or layer theft.
findings.fix: Remove `insecure-registries` or enforce explicit TLS-secured internal registries within the Docker daemon configuration task inside the Ansible playbook.

triage.reason: Insecure container image registries configured without mandatory TLS transport enforcement.

validation.note: Docker daemon config supports insecure-registries via variable expansion.

findings.title: SSH host-key verification disabled
findings.why: Disabling SSH host key checking (`StrictHostKeyChecking=no`) opens the remote deployment up to man-in-the-middle attacks when Ansible connects to manage the remote server.
findings.fix:
Update `inventory/hosts.yml` generation in the deployment script to enable strict checking:
```bash
        ansible_ssh_common_args: '-o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes'
```

triage.reason: SSH host key checking is explicitly disabled, exposing deployments to man-in-the-middle attacks.

validation.note: Ansible deployment script explicitly disables StrictHostKeyChecking=no for root user.

findings.title: Unauthenticated admin/API surface exposed via nginx
findings.why: Exposing administrative tools via the `/mcp` nginx location without authentication allows any unauthenticated external user to invoke sensitive actions like user creation and tenant bootstrapping.

triage.reason: Unauthenticated administrative MCP server tools are exposed publicly via the nginx proxy.

validation.note: Nginx config exposes unauthenticated administrative /mcp endpoints without restriction.

findings.title: Fail-open Kong pre-function allows unauthenticated and unauthorized access to protected routes
findings.why: A fail-open configuration in Kong gateway pre-functions can bypass security filters entirely upon error conditions, exposing protected API endpoints to unauthenticated callers.
findings.fix: Modify the Kong Lua pre-function script to fail closed (deny request by default) if authentication header parsing encounters an exception or missing state.

triage.reason: Fail-open gateway pre-function allows unauthenticated access to protected enterprise routes.

validation.note: Kong pre-function allows unauthenticated access to protected routes if whitelist misconfigured.

findings.title: Container Capabilities Unrestricted
findings.why: Running containers with unrestricted capabilities allows processes inside the container to perform privileged system operations if container isolation is compromised.
findings.fix:
Add `cap_drop: [ALL]` to microservice definitions in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
```

triage.reason: Container capabilities are left unrestricted, violating defense-in-depth principles.

validation.note: Default container capabilities are left unrestricted in service definitions.

findings.title: Security Opt Not Set
findings.why: Omitting security options like `no-new-privileges` permits processes to gain new privileges through `suid` or `sgid` binaries, increasing container breakout impact.
findings.fix:
Add `security_opt` directives to containers in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
```

triage.reason: Missing security hardening options (no-new-privileges) on container deployments.

validation.note: Docker security_opt is not explicitly set on sensitive deployment containers.

findings.title: Container Traffic Not Bound To Host Interface
findings.why: Mapping container ports without binding to a specific host IP defaults to binding on `0.0.0.0`, exposing internal application management ports directly to external networks.
findings.fix:
Explicitly bind published ports to localhost in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:18091:8091"
```

triage.reason: Container service ports are published without strict local interface bindings.

validation.note: Internal backend microservice ports are published directly to host interfaces.

findings.title: Healthcheck Not Set
findings.why: Services without healthchecks configured make it impossible for orchestrators or dependent services to accurately determine if the application is fully ready to accept traffic.
findings.fix:
Add an appropriate healthcheck definition to stateless/stateful services in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/actuator/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
```

triage.reason: Missing healthcheck is a reliability control rather than a direct vulnerability.

validation.note: Migration and utility containers lack healthchecks.

findings.title: Ensure that HTTPS url is used with uri
findings.why: Making internal API calls using cleartext HTTP (`http://127.0.0.1:18200`) over loopback is generally acceptable for local daemon communication, but risks plaintext leakage if network namespace boundaries change.
findings.fix: This is a benign loopback call to OpenBao on the same host where TLS is terminated at the reverse proxy layer. No fix required.

triage.reason: Internal service API calls use cleartext HTTP instead of encrypted HTTPS.

validation.note: OpenBao seal status checks use plain HTTP internally on localhost.

findings.title: File created without an explicit restrictive mode
findings.why: Files created without explicit restrictive permissions can be read or modified by unprivileged local users on the shared host system.
findings.fix:
Ensure Ansible file and template modules specify restrictive file modes:
```yaml
    - name: Create DIGIT directory
      file:
        path: "{{ digit_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0750'
```

triage.reason: Files created without explicit restrictive access modes increase information disclosure risks.

validation.note: Directory and file creation steps lack explicit restrictive modes.

findings.title: Ensure that certificate validation isn't disabled with uri
findings.why: Disabling certificate validation during validation checks defeats TLS trust verification, potentially masking machine-in-the-middle attacks during deployment verification.
findings.fix: Ensure `validate_certs` is only set conditionally when testing sandbox environments without valid public certificates, keeping it strictly `true` for production.

triage.reason: TLS certificate validation can be toggled off, enabling potential interception.

validation.note: Sandbox environments conditionally toggle certificate validation for testing.

findings.title: Privileged Ports Mapped In Container
findings.why: Binding low privileged system ports (< 1024) inside containers is unnecessary when standard high ports can be mapped, occasionally requiring extra capabilities.
findings.fix:
Map container ports to non-privileged ports or bind them explicitly to localhost in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:18080:80"
```

triage.reason: Mapping privileged container ports to high host ports is a benign network configuration.

validation.note: Frontend and overpass services bind privileged container ports to host mappings.

findings.title: Shell pipeline without pipefail (failures go undetected)
findings.why: Shell pipelines without `set -o pipefail` can mask failures in early commands of a pipe, causing Ansible tasks to report success even when critical commands fail.
findings.fix:
Prepend `set -o pipefail;` to multi-command shell scripts in Ansible tasks:
```yaml
    - name: "Turbopass — sweep container when flag is OFF"
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        set -o pipefail
        if docker ps -a --filter name=^turbopass-search$ --format '{{ "{{" }}.Names{{ "}}" }}' | grep -q '^turbopass-search$'; then
          docker rm -f turbopass-search
        fi
```

triage.reason: Shell pipeline executes without pipefail, which may mask underlying command failures.

validation.note: Some shell tasks omit set -o pipefail, potentially masking pipeline errors.

findings.title: Host Namespace is Shared
findings.why: Sharing the host namespace (`pid: host`) allows monitoring containers to inspect all host processes, which expands the attack surface if the monitoring container is compromised.
findings.fix: This is an intentional configuration required for system metrics collection (node-exporter). Ensure the container runs as a non-root user where possible and drop unnecessary capabilities.

triage.reason: Host process namespace sharing is required and read-only for monitoring telemetry agents.

validation.note: Monitoring containers share host pid namespace for metrics collection.

findings.title: Memory Not Limited
findings.why: Containers running without memory limits can consume all available host RAM during load spikes, leading to kernel Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer terminations across other system services.
findings.fix:
Add resource limits to services in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512M
```

triage.reason: Missing container resource memory limits represent reliability controls rather than vulnerabilities.

validation.note: User preferences stack lacks resource memory limits.

findings.title: systemd service runs without hardening (NoNewPrivileges=true)
findings.why: Running systemd service daemons without hardening options like `NoNewPrivileges=true` permits privilege escalation if the application binary is exploited.
findings.fix:
Add hardening directives to the systemd service template in the Ansible playbook:
```ini
[Service]
Type=simple
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=full
ProtectHome=true
```

triage.reason: Systemd service runs without process hardening directives like NoNewPrivileges.

validation.note: Integration test runner systemd service unit lacks NoNewPrivileges=true hardening.

findings.title: systemd service runs without hardening (a non-root User=)
findings.why: Running systemd service daemons without hardening options like `NoNewPrivileges=true` permits privilege escalation if the application binary is exploited.
findings.fix:

[Service]

NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=full
ProtectHome=true

triage.reason: Systemd service runs without process hardening directives like NoNewPrivileges.

validation.note: Integration test runner systemd service unit lacks NoNewPrivileges=true hardening.

findings.title: systemd service runs without hardening (ProtectSystem=)
findings.why: Running systemd service daemons without hardening options like `NoNewPrivileges=true` permits privilege escalation if the application binary is exploited.
findings.fix:
Add hardening directives to the systemd service template in the Ansible playbook:
```ini
[Service]
Type=simple
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=full
ProtectHome=true
```

triage.reason: Systemd service runs without process hardening directives like NoNewPrivileges.

validation.note: Integration test runner systemd service unit lacks NoNewPrivileges=true hardening.

findings.title: nginx is missing the security header: server_tokens off
findings.why: Leaving nginx server tokens enabled leaks exact web server and version information in error pages and headers, assisting attackers in targeting known software vulnerabilities.

triage.reason: Nginx configuration lacks server_tokens off, exposing web server version details.

validation.note: Scanner misfired; server_tokens is managed or configured elsewhere in nginx templates.

findings.title: nginx is missing the security header: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)
findings.why: Leaving nginx server tokens enabled leaks exact web server and version information in error pages and headers, assisting attackers in targeting known software vulnerabilities.

triage.reason: Nginx configuration lacks server_tokens off, exposing web server version details.

validation.note: Scanner misfired; server_tokens is managed or configured elsewhere in nginx templates.

findings.title: nginx is missing the security header: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
findings.why: Leaving nginx server tokens enabled leaks exact web server and version information in error pages and headers, assisting attackers in targeting known software vulnerabilities.

triage.reason: Nginx configuration lacks server_tokens off, exposing web server version details.

validation.note: Scanner misfired; server_tokens is managed or configured elsewhere in nginx templates.

findings.title: Security lint rule disabled in .ansible-lint
findings.why: Disabling important security lint rules in `.ansible-lint` can allow insecure Ansible patterns, file permissions, or syntax errors to slip into production deployments unnoticed.
findings.fix: Remove security rules from the exclusion list in `.ansible-lint` and remediate the flagged tasks to adhere to best-practice guidelines.

triage.reason: Security lint rules are disabled in ansible-lint configuration.

validation.note: Specific ansible-lint rules are intentionally disabled in configuration.

findings.title: Shared Volumes Between Containers
findings.why: Sharing volumes incorrectly between containers can lead to unauthorized data tampering or data leakage between independent microservices.
findings.fix: Ensure shared volumes such as jar files or configuration directories are mounted with read-only flags (`:ro`) in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`.

triage.reason: Shared volumes for static libraries or data directories are expected workload patterns.

validation.note: Elasticsearch shares named volumes safely for state persistence.

findings.title: Cpus Not Limited
findings.why: Unrestricted CPU shares allow a single runaway or compromised container to monopolize host CPU resources, causing denial of service for other microservices.
findings.fix:
Add CPU limits under the deploy block for services in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '0.50'
          memory: 512M
```

triage.reason: Unrestricted CPU limits are reliability controls rather than security vulnerabilities.

validation.note: CPU limits are not explicitly configured on auxiliary compose services.
